options.why: Inbreeding raises the frequency of homozygotes and lowers the frequency of heterozygotes without changing allele frequencies.

options.text: Random mating among all the individuals in the population
options.why: Random mating is a condition for equilibrium, not a violation.

options.text: No mutation, because the alleles are not changed
options.why: The absence of mutation would help keep equilibrium.

items.explanation_en:

A very large population, which prevents chance changes in allele frequencies is incorrect: A large population helps maintain equilibrium and would not cause a heterozygote deficit.
Random mating among all the individuals in the population is incorrect: Random mating is a condition for equilibrium, not a violation.
No mutation, because the alleles are not changed is incorrect: The absence of mutation would help keep equilibrium.
